title: Diffs Are Cheap, Show Me the Trajectory: An Empirical Study of Trajectory-Informed Code Review
abstract: arXiv:2611.31316v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Code review typically starts from the final diff. However, the diff reveals little about how the code was developed. Coding-agent trajectories preserve intermediate decisions, failed attempts, and validation evidence that may assist code review. We systematically investigate whether and how these trajectories can help independent review agents identify problems in the resulting code, beyond inspecting the final diff and repository. We develop a procedure that generates review comments by comparing the initial and merged versions of pull requests, and assess it against withheld human review comments. Using held-out reference implementations as comparison targets for agent-produced code, we construct a dataset linking 339 implementations of 113 DeepSWE tasks with their trajectories and 882 synthetic reference review comments. Across three coding-agent configurations and two review harnesses, we compare diff-only review, full-trajectory acc

translated_title: 差异是廉价的，给我看轨迹：基于轨迹信息的代码审查实证研究
translated_abstract: 代码审查通常从最终的代码差异开始。然而，代码差异几乎无法揭示代码是如何被开发出来的。编码智能体轨迹保留了中间决策、失败的尝试和验证证据，这些信息可能有助于代码审查。我们系统地研究了这些轨迹能否以及如何帮助独立的审查智能体识别最终代码中的问题，而不仅仅是检查最终的代码差异和代码仓库。我们开发了一种通过比较拉取请求的初始版本和合并版本来生成审查意见的流程，并将其与保留的人类审查意见进行对比评估。通过使用留出的参考实现作为智能体生成代码的比较目标，我们构建了一个数据集，将113个DeepSWE任务的339个实现与其轨迹以及882条合成参考审查意见相关联。在三种编码智能体配置和两种审查框架下，我们比较了仅基于差异的审查与基于完整轨迹的审查的表现。
tldr: 该论文通过实证研究系统探索了编码智能体的开发轨迹（包含中间决策、失败尝试和验证证据）能否帮助审查智能体超越仅检查最终代码差异来发现代码问题，并构建了包含339个实现、113个DeepSWE任务轨迹和882条参考审查意见的数据集进行评估。
en_tdlr: This empirical study systematically investigates whether coding-agent trajectories—preserving intermediate decisions, failed attempts, and validation evidence—can help independent review agents identify code problems beyond inspecting final diffs, using a dataset of 339 implementations across 113 DeepSWE tasks with 882 synthetic reference review comments.
